messages:
alex: Hey infra — hitting a weird terraform plan hang in staging, blocking my PR. plan stalls at "Refreshing state..." when the kubernetes provider tries to list RoleBindings. S3 backend shows a lock with LockID `9f2a3b` from yesterday. I ran `terraform force-unlock 9f2a3b` but the plan still hangs and eventually errors with `EOF` / `context deadline exceeded`. Any quick checks I should run?

maria: can you paste a small TF_LOG output and your provider versions? mismatched provider/plugin can deadlock. also try `terraform init -upgrade` first. check KUBECONFIG/token expiry too — kubernetes provider often blocks on auth.

alex: paste log snippet below (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T12:04:02.123Z [INFO]  provider.kubernetes: listing RoleBindings in cluster
2026-03-17T12:04:32.456Z [ERROR] provider.kubernetes: request failed: EOF
2026-03-17T12:06:00.789Z [WARN]  backend.s3: lock exists (LockID=9f2a3b)
2026-03-17T12:06:15.001Z [ERROR] terraform: refresh failed: context deadline exceeded
```

chris: two quick angles: 1) confirm which lock backend we're using — if it's the DynamoDB lock table, run `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "9f2a3b"}}'` to inspect owner/TTL. if it's S3-object-based, check the bucket for a `.lock` key. 2) the kubernetes provider can hang if the kube-apiserver is unreachable from where you're running the plan (CI vs your laptop). run `kubectl --context=staging get ns` from the same host to verify connectivity.

sam: +1 to chris. another quick unblock: if this PR only touches infra module X, you can run `terraform plan -refresh=false -target=module.X` to skip the full refresh and get the plan for your change. it's not ideal long-term (you skip drift detection) but ok for short PR unblock. also try `terraform workspace select staging` to ensure workspace mismatch isn't the cause.

maria: to add — if you do `-refresh=false`, make a state backup first: `terraform state pull > state-backup.json`. and schedule a proper full refresh after the PR merge. long-term we should add provider request timeouts and better error messages in our provider wrapper: e.g. set `request_timeout = \"60s\"` or use the exec plugin with cached tokens.

alex: thanks all — i'll try `init -upgrade`, confirm kube connectivity from the CI runner, and then try `plan -refresh=false -target=module.myservice` with a state backup. will report back. :thumbsup:
